Samhain (se pronuncia aproximadamente “s: Samhain (pronounced roughly “SOW-in”) is a festival of Celtic origin that was celebrated between October 31 and November 1, halfway between the autumn equinox and the winter solstice. It marked the end of the harvest, a time of turning inward, and the start of the dark half of the year. A widely held, symbolic belief says that around these dates the “veil” between the world of the living and the world of the dead grows thinner. Much of what we now know as Halloween comes from Samhain and the eve of All Saints' Day.
